title: Switch Cases & Template Helpers 🔀
description: Use *ngSwitch, ng-template, and ng-container for cleaner conditional views.

slides.title: When If/Else Gets Messy 🤯
slides.content:
# *ngSwitch

Sometimes you have multiple conditions, and nesting `*ngIf`/`else` becomes hard to read. Angular provides `*ngSwitch` – like a JavaScript `switch` statement in the template.

Three parts:
* `[ngSwitch]` – an attribute binding on a container element, evaluating the expression.
* `*ngSwitchCase` – a structural directive that displays the element when the value matches.
* `*ngSwitchDefault` – displayed when no case matches.

quizData.question: Which directive marks the container element for a switch block?
quizData.explanation: `[ngSwitch]` is an attribute binding that sets the switch expression on the container.

slides.title: ng-template: The Hidden Blueprint 🕶️
slides.content:
`<ng-template>` is a fundamental Angular element. It’s never rendered directly; instead, it’s a template that can be stamped into the DOM by structural directives.

* `*ngIf`, `*ngFor`, `*ngSwitchCase` all use `<ng-template>` under the hood.
* You can reference it with a template reference variable (`#myTemplate`).
* Use it with `ngTemplateOutlet` to dynamically render a template.

Think of it as a reusable piece of view that you can define once and use multiple times.
